subject: general
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

______ is going to take the responsibility for this failure?
solution:
The correct answer is **"Who"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us explore the meanings of the given options:
 
 
• **"Whom"** is used to refer to the object of a verb or preposition. We use **"whom"** when it is receiving the action.
 
• **Who: **If the question can be answered with a subject pronoun (he, she, it, or they), use "**who."**
 
• **Which: **We use **"which"** in questions as a determiner and interrogative pronoun to ask for specific information
 
• **"Whose"** is a possessive pronoun and we use it when we're asking (or telling) to whom something belongs.
 
 
 
• Here the blank needs to be filled up by the **subject pronoun** which is **"Who"**.
 
• According to the given sentence, **Who** will be held accountable for this **failure**?
 
• So, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct sentence:** ***Who__** is going to take the responsibility for this failure?*

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__**

 
• When a person being described is **the subject** of a sentence or follows a **preposition**, the word "**whom"** should be used.
 
• In order to ask for **specific information**, we utilize the **interrogative pronoun "which"** as a determiner in questions.
 
• A **possessive pronoun** is **whose**. Use it to determine whom something belongs to when asking (or telling) someone.
